facts.fact: The National Treasury allocated Sh12.7 billion to the digital superhighway programme in the FY2025/26 budget estimates presented by Treasury CS John Mbadi.
facts.system: Digital superhighway programme, FY2025/26 budget

facts.fact: The FY2025/26 allocation of Sh12.7 billion for the digital superhighway programme is a 22 per cent reduction from Sh16.3 billion in FY2024/25.
facts.system: Digital superhighway programme, FY2025/26 budget

facts.fact: The FY2025/26 budget allocates Sh3.1 billion to the Konza Data Centre and Smart City project, down from Sh5.2 billion in FY2024/25.
facts.system: Konza Data Centre and Smart City project, FY2025/26 budget

facts.fact: The FY2025/26 budget raises funding for the Kenya Digital Economy Acceleration project to Sh3.7 billion from Sh2.8 billion in FY2024/25; the document does not say how the project is financed.
facts.system: Kenya Digital Economy Acceleration project, FY2025/26 budget

note: Facts are budget-day reporting of proposed estimates; no commitment statement beyond a general assurance of targeted investments and public-private partnerships.

facts.fact: The Universal Service Fund, administered by the Communications Authority, funded the Digital Superhighway backbone and metro fibre procurement (tenders expected to cost over Sh15 billion per the petitioner), and a 1 October 2024 Attorney-General advisory was relied on by the CA in processing payments; the document does not name the law assigning the fund, and the High Court quashed the advisory on 2026-09-04 but did not nullify the contracts.
facts.system: Universal Service Fund

note: Draft Administration of Universal Service Fund Regulations 2026 are only proposed (validation forum 15-17 September 2026) and would revoke the 2010 Universal Access and Service Regulations; no collection or payment is shown, so no acted fact.

facts.fact: The Communications Authority is implementing a Digital Skilling Project through its Universal Service Fund to train 120,000 people across 19 counties over three years; no amount or founding law is given.
facts.system: Universal Service Fund Digital Skilling Project

note: Stakeholder site visit by the Universal Service Advisory Council; no amount, date of payment or funding act stated, so no fact.
Article on Starlink in Nigeria and other markets; names Kenya only for Starlink subscriber numbers and licence conditions, nothing on Kenya's budget, fund or levy for digital programmes.

facts.fact: Treasury CS John Mbadi's budget speech proposed KSh 8.6 billion for the digital economy and creative industry (the digital superhighway package) for FY2026/27.
facts.system: Kenya national budget FY2026/27, digital economy and creative industry allocation

facts.fact: The FY2026/27 allocation of KSh 8.6 billion for digital economy and creative industry is lower than the KSh 12.7 billion set aside for the ICT sector in the 2025/26 budget.
facts.system: Kenya national budget FY2026/27, digital economy and creative industry allocation

facts.fact: KSh 4.3 billion of the FY2026/27 allocation goes to the World Bank-backed Kenya Digital Economy Acceleration Project (part-financed by the Bank; the article does not say it is paid wholly by it).
facts.system: Kenya Digital Economy Acceleration Project (KDEAP), FY2026/27 budget

facts.fact: The KDEAP allocation rose by KSh 600 million, from KSh 3.7 billion in 2025/26 to KSh 4.3 billion in 2026/27.
facts.system: Kenya Digital Economy Acceleration Project (KDEAP), FY2026/27 budget

facts.fact: The FY2026/27 original estimates (Programme Based Budget, Vote 1122) appropriate KES 12,763,784,217 to the State Department for ICT and Digital Economy; the vote was restructured, with cyber and data protection given their own programme.
facts.system: Vote 1122 State Department for ICT and Digital Economy, FY2026/27

facts.fact: The budget-day digital superhighway and creative economy package fell to KSh 8.6bn for FY2026/27, the second consecutive cut after KSh 16.3bn and KSh 12.7bn; KSh 4.3bn of it is the World Bank-backed KDEAP.
facts.system: Digital superhighway and creative economy package, FY2026/27

facts.fact: Supplementary I to the FY2025/26 budget revised Vote 1122 (State Department for ICT and Digital Economy) to KES 12,215,127,932, with the ICT and BPO Development (Konza/KAIST capital transfer) line cut 59%.
